key_insight: The paper introduces quantum probabilistic local differential privacy, a relaxed privacy notion that allows rare spectral violations, and derives its structural properties and hypothesis-testing sample complexity bounds.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical framework for designing quantum privacy mechanisms with quantifiable failure probability, especially relevant to quantum machine learning and private quantum inference pipelines.
method: Define a probabilistic relaxation of quantum local differential privacy with a low-probability violation event
Analyze structural properties under tensor-product composition and unitary post-processing
Relate privacy guarantees to hockey-stick divergence and quantum Neyman-Pearson testing to derive sample complexity bounds
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical results only, including structural analysis, depolarizing-noise characterizations, and sample complexity bounds for asymmetric and symmetric quantum hypothesis testing.
watch_item: The privacy notion is not closed under arbitrary quantum-channel post-processing and is not convex in general, so implementation must carefully control allowed transformations.
paper_title: Quantum Probabilistic Local Differential Privacy: Structural Properties and Sample Complexity Bounds
